title: Indian Ocean 10-Year Landmark Thermal & Sea-Level Record (2016–2025)
source: NASA MODIS Aqua SST, Jason-3 & Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich Altimetry
coords: LAT: 08.40° N | LON: 73.10° E (EQUATORIAL INDIAN OCEAN / ARABIAN SEA)
theoryOverview: Over the 2016–2025 decade, NASA radar altimeters (Jason-3 and Sentinel-6) and MODIS Aqua infrared radiometers documented unprecedented upper-ocean heat uptake in the Indian Ocean. Because water expands as it warms (thermosteric expansion) and receives meltwater from polar ice sheets (barystatic rise), regional sea levels rose from +79.2mm to +112.4mm above the 1993 baseline.

records.explanation: 2016 Super El Niño & Coral Bleaching Landmark: 29.1°C SST and +79.2mm sea-level anomaly trigger global reef stress.
records.theory: Extreme Indo-Pacific Warm Pool heat accumulation suppressed upwelling, causing widespread thermal bleaching.

records.explanation: 2017 Post-El Niño Equilibration: Slight surface cooling to 28.8°C, but subsurface heat pushes sea level to +82.4mm.
records.theory: Heat mixed downward into the 0–700m thermocline layer continues steric expansion despite mild surface cooling.

records.explanation: 2018 Arabian Sea Cyclone Intensification: 29.0°C waters and +86.5mm level fuel rapid tropical cyclone spin-up.
records.theory: High Tropical Cyclone Heat Potential (TCHP) provides latent heat energy that prevents storm-induced cold-wake cooling.

records.explanation: 2019 Extreme Positive Indian Ocean Dipole (+IOD): +0.4°C jump to 29.4°C! Western basin sea level hits +91.0mm.
records.theory: Strong easterly wind anomalies piled warm water against East Africa and the Arabian Sea, triggering severe regional floods.

records.explanation: 2020 Sentinel-6 Launch Milestone: 29.3°C SST and +94.6mm rise calibrated by next-gen radar interferometry.
records.theory: Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich dual-frequency Poseidon-4 altimeter confirms accelerating 3.6 mm/yr regional rise rate.

records.explanation: 2021 La Niña Heat Redistribution: 29.2°C surface temperature as Indonesian Throughflow pumps warm water into basin (+98.1mm).
records.theory: Strengthened Pacific trade winds push warm western Pacific waters through the Indonesian archipelago into the Indian Ocean.

records.explanation: 2022 100mm Threshold Crossed: Regional sea-level rise breaches +101.8mm above 1993 baseline at 29.5°C.
records.theory: Combined thermosteric expansion (55%) and glacier/ice-sheet mass influx (45%) push coastal tide gauges past 10cm.

records.explanation: 2023 Global Marine Heatwave Record: 29.7°C extreme SST anomaly and +105.6mm sea-level surge trigger alarm harmonics!
records.theory: Developing El Niño + reduced marine cloud aerosols caused record net downward shortwave radiation into the ocean mixed layer.

records.explanation: 2024 Persistent Basin-Wide Heatwave: 29.8°C SST and +109.2mm rise; intense stratification traps subsurface heat.
records.theory: Weakened wind-driven vertical mixing prevents cooler deep water from reaching the surface, locking in high acoustic pitch.

records.explanation: 2025 Decadal Peak Anomaly: 29.9°C SST & +112.4mm cumulative rise! Maximum FM pad chord & rogue wave filter sweep.
records.theory: Indian Ocean heat content reaches all-time observational high, driving maximum frequency modulation and alert overtones.
